newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: S.E. Asia currency turmoil slows with eyes on baht.
newsitem.headline: S.E. Asia currency turmoil slows with eyes on baht.

text.p: Southeast Asia's battered currencies crawled cautiously into the new week on Monday after a meeting of top regional central bankers gave the market pause for thought.
Dealers said Friday's meeting of 11 central banks in Shanghai was thoroughly uninspiring and its joint statement little more than rhetoric.

But they said the statement's promise that members of the group would work with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) to find answers to their economic problems shifted attention back to Thailand, whose problems triggered weeks of currency mayhem.
Thai Finance Minister Thanong Bidaya said on Monday he was seeking IMF advice this week ahead of an economic revival package due by August 5.
He said economic ministers would discuss a rescue package for the economy, but the talks would not cover the question of borrowing from the IMF.
Dealers saw little cause for optimism in the potential contents of the government's package, especially in the absence of IMF aid.
"What kind of package can you come out with if you have no money? If anything, it'll be more restrictive rather than pro-growth," a Singapore dealer said.
"I can't seen any other packages, aside from borrowing from the IMF," he added.
But another Singapore dealer said the baht showed a slight upward bias on news that Thailand would be seeking IMF advice.
Activity was limited to commercial flows as most players refrained from taking positions until there was a clearer indication of what sort of assistance Thailand would take from the IMF.
"The baht drifted in a very tight band of around 32.00-32.300 this morning. I noticed some exporters started selling dollars, but in very modest amount," a U.S. bank dealer in Bangkok said.

A Singapore dealer said the dollar's topside looked capped around 32.10/15 baht in offshore markets. "I don't know if the central bank is up there. But the usual seller from Hong Kong is around," he said without elaboration.
In Indonesia, the rupiah had a slow morning, remaining within a relatively narrow range of 2,600-2,615 to the dollar.

A U.S. bank dealer in Jakarta said operators were reluctant to sell dollars for fear of further turmoil in regional markets, while buyers were discouraged by the dollar's high levels and possible central bank actions.
Spot rupiah was quoted at 2,605/15 at 0420 GMT, unchanged from its opening levels.
The central bank's recent moves to tighten money market liquidity also spurred caution, dealers said.
The Malaysian ringgit and Singapore dollar were expected to trade in 50-point ranges against the U.S. dollar.
Dealers said interest was limited as players awaited developments in Thailand, but both currencies remained under pressure from recent uncertainty in the region.
The dollar's surge to a 92-month high of 1.8465 marks in morning trade was also cited as a factor weighing on the ringgit and Sing dollar.
In the Philippines, the central bank sold dollars at around 28.50 pesos in the face of heavy dollar demand from importers, Manila traders said.
The peso was at 28.460/550 at 0420 GMT against its Friday close at 28.47.
The central bank effectively slashed the overnight borrowing rate to 22 percent from 25 percent in the third such cut since the peso's de facto devaluation on July 11.
